name: Abraham Ortelius, Africae Tabula Nova, 1570 (Theatrum Orbis Terrarum; this impression 1572)
note: 12444x9188, hand-coloured. S. Matheo is drawn west of Annobon just south of the equator as an orange-washed island of 65 x 109 px — a boot, notched on the west, with a speck of an islet off its north end. Chosen by Etienne in October 2026 over Mercator's Africa of 1595 (the same boot and islet in red, ~40 x 65 px), Blaeu's Africae nova descriptio of 1630 (a different shape, a blank sliver of ~60 x 20 px) and the story's own plate (a late-18th-century French sheet, ~15 px in the copy we have, source unidentified). The Theatrum was the best-selling atlas in Europe for decades and Mercator repeats this shape, so it is the influential depiction as well as the largest scan.
extraction_note: --mode red: the wash is orange, R-(G+B)/2 > 40 isolates it at 3619 px against a stippled parchment sea. The islet to the north is uncoloured, so the wash cannot carry it: `--islet` seals its ink ring (grey < 110, closing radius 4-6, a plateau at 212-222 px) and keeps the pale core as a satellite. At radius 8 and above the closing fuses the sea hatching above it and the core leaks to 1272 px.
